German courted a waitress for a long time.
And in the end she agreed.
But suddenly a cook walked in there.
And we already saw what happened next.
He is just a total psycho!
And what happened to him after that?
He received a suspended sentence back then.
In Latvia he is on the blacklist.
Is it that easy to make him lose his temper?

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: in questions: а вдруг...? = and what if...?
А вдруг... = what if. Core Russian adv meaning 'suddenly; all of a sudden' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level?
Suddenly it began to rain.

examples.text: Почему он вдруг сравнялся? Мы шли впереди на десять процентов!
examples.trans: Why did it suddenly draw level? We were ten percent ahead!

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: See?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: See you!
I have a meeting.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'вести'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to escort out / lead out'.

examples.text: Посмотри, какой ты дерзкий! Может, тебя отсюда вывести?
examples.trans: Look how cheeky you are! Maybe I should escort you out of here?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и вывести вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to escort out on time.

related.gloss: not to to escort out (negated infinitive)

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.
In a list or a story. Core Russian adv meaning 'next; further' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: All right. Next.
What's next?

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.
Core Russian prep meaning 'until, before; up to' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Goodbye!

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!

зайти.gloss: to come in, to drop in

meanings.en: to come in, to step in
meanings.note: Into a room. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'заходить'.
To visit briefly. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come in, to drop in', paired with 'заходить'.

examples.trans: Come in, please!
I'll drop by in the evening.

examples.text: Ну, как хочешь. Лидия Алексеевна, зайдите, пожалуйста!
examples.trans: Well, as you like. Lidia Alekseyevna, come in, please!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.

examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, I already know. The town hall called me.

meanings.note: concluding sum or recap of an event

examples.trans: Let's sum up the first week.

examples.text: В итоге все остались очень довольны.
examples.trans: In the end everyone remained very satisfied.

examples.text: Подведём итоги твоей первой рабочей недели.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'blacklist', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: В Латвии он в чёрном списке.

meanings.note: Impersonal predicate or adverb. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Да это легко. Схватил собачку в парке и побежал.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to get, to receive', paired with 'получать'.

examples.text: А кто их получит? Те, кто сидит повыше?
examples.trans: And who will get it? The people who sit higher up?

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to agree', paired with 'соглашаться'.

examples.trans: Admit it / Don't you agree, that's much better.

examples.text: Это гораздо лучше, чем двенадцать лет. Согласитесь?
examples.trans: That's much better than twelve years. Don't you agree?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'list' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is my list.

meanings.note: Второй срок = a second term. Common masculine noun meaning 'term, period' in everyday Russian.
Common masculine noun meaning 'term, period' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: At the start of a question. Core Russian part meaning 'so, then; like that' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to suspense'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: Chef, come on, do not keep us in suspense.
It happened in Riga.

meanings.note: Directional adverb. Core Russian adv meaning 'there, thither (motion)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я знаю! Хочешь, сейчас и тебя туда увезут?
examples.trans: I know! Do you want them to take you there too right now?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: условный срок = a suspended sentence

Условный знак = an agreed signal. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('conditional; agreed; suspended (sentence)').

examples.trans: He got a suspended sentence.
It's an agreed signal.

examples.text: А я тебе делаю условный срок. Плюс ты забираешь все деньги Вики.
examples.trans: And I get you a suspended sentence. Plus you take all of Vika's money.

ухаживать.gloss: to court, to woo; to look after

meanings.en: to court, to pay court to
meanings.note: + за + instrumental. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to court, to woo; to look after'.

meanings.en: to look after, to care for
meanings.note: + за + instrumental. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to court, to woo; to look after'.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал.
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once.
She looks after her sick mother.

examples.text: Он за мной после концерта ухаживал. В Москву звал замуж!
examples.trans: He courted me after a concert once. He asked me to marry him and come to Moscow!

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!

meanings.note: Informal. Borrowed from French 'chef' (head, leader, from Latin 'caput'); in Russian kitchen culture 'шеф' is the standard form of address for the executive head chef.

examples.trans: Cleverly thought out, boss!
The boss signed the order.
The chef is in the kitchen.
